message.content: I have full context. The kernel evaluates a 64-step linear recurrence in a Triton kernel that deliberately rounds the intermediate state to float16 each step (line 16), against a float64 reference with a tight 0.002 relative-L2 tolerance. The input generator builds an orthogonal-similar matrix with eigenvalues around 0.875–0.969, and state magnitudes ~0.1 — exactly the regime where fp16 rounding (~1e-3 relative) per step can accumulate. I'll record a description update.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Inputs are fixed, public: matrix (16,16) float32 from a Hadamard-similar of an upper-triangular matrix with diagonals in {0.875..0.96875} plus small off-diagonals, initial (16,) ~N(0,0.1) float32, drive (64,16) ~N(0,0.1) float32; seeds PCG64(20260923) and PCG64(202009).", "Reference is the exact float64 recurrence state = matrix @ state + drive[t] over 64 steps on the float32 inputs.", "Output must be a finite float32 vector of shape (16,) with relative L2 error <= 0.002 versus the reference (denominator max(||ref||_2, 0.004)).", "Intermediate approximation is explicitly allowed; only the final vector's error matters. Target device is an NVIDIA T4. Only this fixed workload is in scope.", "Matrix spectral radius ~0.875-0.969 < 1, so the state norm stays moderate (initial O(0.4), drive O(0.1) contributions decay geometrically); the final state norm is likely dominated by early drive terms and is probably O(0.1-1)."], "kernel_model": ["Single Triton program (grid (1,)) loads the full 16x16 matrix into registers, loads initial state, and runs a 64-step unrolled loop: next = matrix @ state + drive[t], computed as tl.sum of fp32 products with enable_fp_fusion=False.", "After each step, the state is explicitly quantized to float16 and back to float32 (line 16: next_state.to(tl.float16).to(tl.float32)), introducing up to ~2^-11 relative rounding per step.", "The final state is stored as float32 into a (16,) output; the fp16 quantization of step 64 is included before the store.", "Matrix loaded as native float32 (no cast); products and the tl.sum reduction are fp32; the only lossy operation is the per-step fp16 state round-trip.", "run() is hardcoded to N=16, STEPS=64, matching the workload exactly; no shape checks or fallbacks."], "risk_map</arg_key>[\"Per-step fp16 quantization (unit roundoff 2^-11 ~ 4.88e-4) accumulated over 64 steps: naive bound ~64*4.88e-4 ~ 3% relative error, but error dynamics are matrix-dependent (amplified by modes with eigenvalue near 0.97, damped by smaller ones), so the actual error may or may not stay under 0.002 — this is the central question and needs a runtime measurement.\", \"fp16 has ~3 decimal digits of mantissa; state components ~O(0.1) get absolute rounding up to ~6e-5 per step; error feeds back through matrix and drive, so error growth is roughly geometric with rate ~0.94 and saturation at (rounding*0.94)/(1-0.94) ~ 15x single-step error for the largest eigenvalue mode — potentially ~1e-3 relative, near the tolerance boundary.\", \"tl.sum reduction order and fp32 accumulation are deterministic but differ from float64 reference; that alone contributes only ~1e-7-level error, negligible compared to fp16 effect.\", \"Subnormal/overflow: state magnitudes ~0.1 are far from fp16 extremes (max 65504), so no overflow/underflow risk in scope.\", \"Shape/generation mismatch: none expected; run hardcodes the exact workload dimensions.\"]</arg_value><arg_key>scope_notes": "In scope: only run(*make_inputs()) on the fixed seeded workload, on a T4, with the stated relative-L2 metric. Out of scope: alternative inputs, other tolerances, other devices, general recurrence correctness.\", \"The contract permits intermediate approximation, so fp16 per-step rounding is legal per se; the verdict hinges solely on whether the final relative L2 error <= 0.002 for this exact input.\"]", "open_questions": ["Actual final relative L2 error of run(*make_inputs()) vs the float64 reference — needs an Experimenter probe (the analytic bound straddles the 0.002 threshold, so it cannot be decided from source alone).", "Whether the fp16 round of the last step (before store) plus accumulation across 64 steps lands under or over tolerance for the largest-eigenvalue (0.96875) mode."], "summary": "Described case_e: a 16x16, 64-step linear recurrence kernel that runs the loop in fp32 but quantizes the state to fp16 at every step, judged against a float64 reference with a 0.002 relative-L2 budget. The fp16-per-step quantization is the dominant risk surface; whether accumulated error stays within 0.002 is close to the tolerance boundary and needs runtime measurement."}
